clips.send: A friend who just inherited money sends this to someone about to blow it - anxiety that money without the right mindset disappears as fast as it came.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau tells a story from 1979: a wealthy man in a Rolls Royce, handmade suit, Rolex on his wrist. Kevin half-joked, "If I had your money, I'd have your attitude too."

The man almost snapped at him - out of love, because he knew that attitude would keep Kevin broke.

His answer: the money doesn't give you the attitude. The attitude gives you the money. You hold it while you're flat broke, for weeks or years, before the money shows up.

That's also why 98% of lottery winners go bankrupt - they got the money without the attitude, and it didn't stick.

Which one are you building first: the attitude, or waiting on the money?

clips.send: A guy chasing his first $100K sends this to a friend who thinks a million dollars means he's made it - awe at how small 'rich' really still is.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says the word "millionaire" doesn't mean what people think it means.

Back in 1910, being a millionaire meant something closer to $100 million in today's money, and it was in cash, not real estate you can't easily sell.

Put $100 million in the bank at 8-10% and it throws off roughly $1 million a month. No job. No business. No meetings. The money just lands every month for the rest of your life.

That's the actual definition of financial freedom Kevin uses: money working so you don't have to.

By that measure, how far are you really from "rich"?

#kevintrudeau #financialfreedom #moneymindset #wealthmindset #millionaire #richhabits

clips.send: A guy grinding 60-hour weeks sends this to a friend saving every paycheck - anxiety that he's optimizing the wrong decade of his life.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau describes what financial freedom actually felt like day to day.

No banking app back then. He'd call his banker from wherever he was in the world and ask one question: how much came in today?

One day it was $87,500. The next, $24,000. Didn't matter where he was, Bellagio, Italy included - American Express could hand him cash on the spot.

That's the picture behind the phrase "money working for you": it shows up whether or not you're paying attention to it.

What would you do with a day if a deposit like that was already on its way?
